author: Today I Found Out
description: On October 14, 2012, Austrian skydiver Felix Baumgartner opened the hatch on his pressurized balloon gondola and gazed down at the earth some 128,000 feet below. After making some final adjustments to his pressure suit, parachute, and cameras, he stepped to the edge of the hatch and leaped out into space. After 42 seconds he had reached a speed of 843 mph, becoming the first human to break the sound barrier without a vehicle. Baumgartner continued to fall for 3 minutes, 34 seconds until his parachute deployed at an altitude of 8,200ft. Then, approximately 5 minutes after leaving the balloon, Baumgartner touched down safely in the desert near Roswell, New Mexico. The Stratos jump, a publicity stunt sponsored by energy drink manufacturer Red Bull, was watched by over 9.5 million people online and resulted in Baumgartner clinching three official skydiving records: highest jump altitude, highest vertical speed, and longest free-fall without a drogue chute.
